title: Rebase project manifest
description: Declares which runtime major a project targets and which apps this repository contributes to it. Topology only — tables, security rules, hooks and functions stay in TypeScript under backend/.

$schema.description: URL of this schema, for editor completion.

rebase.description: Runtime contract major this project targets, as a semver range (e.g. "^1"). The platform upgrades patches and minors underneath a project; it never crosses a major. Named "rebase" so that "runtime" means exactly one thing — who owns the backend process.

apps.description: Apps this repository contributes, keyed by name. The key is the app's identity within the project.

propertyNames.description: Lowercase alphanumeric with dashes — the name appears in URLs.

type.description: Which kind of app this is. Everything else an entry may declare follows from it.

telemetry.description: Repository-wide opt-out from anonymous CLI usage sharing. Only `false` does anything: it suppresses sharing for everyone who clones this repository, overriding each developer's own opt-in. `true` is deliberately ignored — this file is committed, so a `true` here would answer a privacy question on behalf of every colleague who later clones the repo. Individuals opt in with `rebase telemetry enable`.

relativePath.description: A path relative to the directory holding rebase.json, and staying inside it. The old pattern only refused a leading "../", so a bare ".." passed the editor and was then rejected by the CLI.

buildContextPath.description: A Docker build context, relative to the directory holding rebase.json. This is the one path here allowed to point ABOVE the project (".."), because it names something Rebase hands to `docker build` rather than something it reads. In a workspace repository the context is normally the workspace root — the lockfile and the sibling packages a Dockerfile copies do not live beside rebase.json.

backendApp.description: The tables, hooks and functions that define the project's API. Exactly one per project.

runtime.description: Who owns the process. "managed": the platform runtime image boots this project's bundle. "custom": this repository builds its own image and entrypoint. Independent of where it runs — both run on Rebase Cloud and both self-host.

tables.description: Directory whose index.ts exports the project's tables and views (defineTable, defineAuthTable, defineView) and, optionally, defaultRls. Default "backend/schema". When it has no index.ts, tables are introspected from the live database at boot. Replaces "config" and "usersCollection", which the CLI refuses — run the collections-to-tables codemod.

crons.description: Directory of cron job definitions. Default "backend/crons".

schema.description: Generated Drizzle schema module. Default "backend/src/schema.generated.ts". Not the tables directory — that is "tables".

registerDatabase.description: Type server-side data from the generated Database. When true, every `rebase generate-sdk` (`rebase dev`'s included, and the first one on a fresh clone) writes the types and the Register declaration to backend/generated/. `rebase generate-sdk --register` sets it. Default false.

dockerfile.description: Custom runtime only. Dockerfile path. Default "Dockerfile".

context.description: Custom runtime only. Directory passed to `docker build` as the build context, relative to the directory holding rebase.json. Default ".". May point above the project — ".." for an app inside a workspace whose Dockerfile copies the root lockfile. `dockerfile` stays relative to rebase.json either way; it is re-expressed against this when a build command is printed.

port.description: Custom runtime only. Port the container listens on. Default 8080.

staticApp.description: A pre-built client bundle — an SPA or static site — served at its declared path. The admin panel is one of these.

build.description: Command producing `output`. Run from the repository root, with REBASE_APP_BASE set from `path`.

anyOf.description: A path, e.g. "/admin": the app answers on every hostname the project is served on.
An https URL, e.g. "https://admin.example.com": the app answers only on that hostname, at the path after it ("/" when there is none).

path.description: Where this app is served: a path, e.g. "/admin", or an https URL that also gives it a hostname of its own, e.g. "https://admin.example.com" or "https://admin.example.com/cms". The path part is a build-time input as well as a serving concern: the app must be built for it (Vite's `base`, from REBASE_APP_BASE), or every asset 404s. A URL takes no port, query or fragment — the platform serves each hostname over TLS — and on Rebase Cloud the deploy registers its hostname on the project, which goes live once its DNS records verify. No two static apps may share a hostname and path (an app with no hostname is its own case; on a hostname, the app naming it wins at an equal path). On every hostname, the path part must not be one the backend owns (/api, /health, /healthz, /livez, /readyz, /metrics) — the API's routes answer first, so an app declared there would answer the API's requests with its own index.html.

spa.description: Serve index.html for unmatched paths under `path` (client-side routing).

cms.description: Where this app mounts the Rebase CMS, as a URL path — the address you would type, not a path relative to `path`. The CMS is a component inside your own app, so its address is a client-side route that nothing on the server can observe: declaring it here is what lets Rebase Cloud and `rebase apps list` link straight to it. Must be the path part of `path` or something beneath it. Always a path, even when `path` is a URL: the CMS is served on this app's own hostname. Omit it if this app does not mount the CMS.

routes.description: Paths on this app's address that a custom function answers instead of the build — a sitemap, a feed, a server-rendered page. The function's response, whatever its content type, is served at the route's path, on this app's hostname when `path` names one; the function sees the request as if called at /api/functions/<name>. The most specific route wins (an exact path before a wildcard, a longer wildcard before a shorter), and a route wins over a file of the same path in the build. Served by the backend this app is folded into: a static app deployed on its own has no functions to call.

path.description: The URL path, absolute and inside the app's `path`: exact, e.g. "/sitemap.xml", or a prefix ending in "/*", e.g. "/blog/*", which matches "/blog" and everything beneath it and hands the function the rest ("/blog/hello" → its "/hello" route). No segment may start with ".", and no path the backend owns (/api, /health, /healthz, /livez, /readyz, /metrics) may be routed.

function.description: The custom function that answers it, by name — its file name without the extension: "sitemap" for functions/sitemap.ts, served at /api/functions/sitemap.

frameAncestors.description: Origins allowed to frame this app, besides its own, written into the `frame-ancestors` directive of its Content-Security-Policy. Without it the app is served with `frame-ancestors 'self'`. Each entry is one origin: https with a hostname and an optional port, or http for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1]. No wildcards, paths or keywords — 'self' is always included.

redirects.description: Requests this app answers with a redirect instead of a file — moved pages, a renamed section, a whole hostname sent to another. Checked in declaration order, before the build's files; the first match answers. The request's query string is kept unless `to` has one of its own. A path `routes` sends to a function is the function's, and is not redirected. An app at "https://example.com" whose only redirect is { "from": "/:path*", "to": "https://www.example.com/:path*" } sends the bare domain to www.

from.description: The path it matches, absolute and inside the app's `path` (the path part, when `path` is a URL): literal segments, ":name" for one segment, and ":name*" as the last segment for the rest of the path, none included. A trailing slash on the request is ignored; matching is case-sensitive. No empty segment, no trailing slash, no segment starting with ".", and a ":" only to start a parameter. Never under a path the backend owns (/api, /health, /healthz, /livez, /readyz, /metrics). A query string is matched with `query`, a hostname with `host`.

to.description: Where it sends the request: a path on the same address, e.g. "/new", or an absolute http:// or https:// URL. ":name" and ":name*" are replaced by what `from` captured, in the path and query only, and must be parameters `from` declares. A redirect to a path its own `from` matches again is refused, since it would loop.

status.description: The redirect's status: 301 or 308 for a permanent move (308 keeps the method), 302 or 307 for a temporary one (307 keeps the method).

host.description: Only for requests to this hostname, lowercase, with no scheme, port or path. On an app whose `path` names a hostname, it can only be that one.

notHost.description: Only for requests to any hostname but this one, lowercase, with no scheme, port or path: what vercel.json writes as `missing` with "type": "host". Not with `host`, and never the hostname the app's `path` names.

query.description: Only for requests whose query string holds each of these parameters with exactly this value, compared after decoding. "" matches the parameter present with no value (?k or ?k=); there is no wildcard.

cleanUrls.description: Serve `x.html` at /x, and answer /x.html with a 308 to /x, query kept: /privacidad serves privacidad.html, /legal/terms serves legal/terms.html. A file or directory of the request's exact name is served first, and an index.html redirects to its directory (/docs/index.html to /docs/).
